trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha has turned mildly softer after two weeks of flat-lining. USD/ZMW moved from 20.2630 (4 Nov) to 20.3157 (6 Nov, open.er-api.com), a 0.26% depreciation, and the whole cross-currency basket cost more kwacha over the same two days: sterling +0.65% (27.3598), euro +0.60% (22.8175), rand +1.37% (1.2400) and pula +1.05% (1.4323), while the yuan was flat at 3.0386. That broad-based pattern points to genuine kwacha selling rather than one cross moving. Support still comes from record copper output and elevated copper prices, reserves near US$5.5bn, a near-complete debt restructuring, the US$1.47bn IMF staff-level agreement and the Lobito rail corridor advancing. The offsets are month-start corporate USD demand, rising fuel import costs flagged in November commentary, a materially easier policy stance after the 30 September MPR cut to 10.75%, and the 10% copper-concentrate export duty. Watch whether 20.35 holds; a clean break opens the 20.50 area.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 19.60–20.60 range. Copper earnings and IMF programme inflows supportive; softer policy, fuel imports and month-start USD demand the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.80–20.60 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings through the Lobito/export-logistics build-out, and the pace of further BoZ easing.
